  1. Hash the key into an integer.
  2. Take that integer modulo the bucket count to get an index.
  3. Walk the bucket, comparing stored keys for equality.
  4. Return the matching value, or report that the key is absent.

  ┌───────────┬─────────┬────────────┐
  │ Operation │ Average │ Worst case │
  ├───────────┼─────────┼────────────┤
  │ Insert    │ O(1)    │ O(n)       │
  ├───────────┼─────────┼────────────┤
  │ Get       │ O(1)    │ O(n)       │
  ├───────────┼─────────┼────────────┤
  │ Remove    │ O(1)    │ O(n)       │
  └───────────┴─────────┴────────────┘

  Here is a short example using Rust's standard HashMap:

  use std::collections::HashMap;

  fn main() {
      let mut ages: HashMap<&str, u32> = HashMap::new();
      ages.insert("alice", 31);
      ages.insert("bob", 27);

      if let Some(age) = ages.get("alice") {
          println!("alice is {age}");
      }
  }
